title: A specified divided row gives a finite biproduct pivot block
statement: Let C be a preadditive category with finite biproducts and binary biproducts. Let P be an object, f:P^n→P^t, and i∈Fin t, j∈Fin n. Write p=ι_j f π_i. Suppose q_k:P→P satisfies q_k p=ι_k f π_i for every k. Then there are m<n and s, isomorphisms P^n≅P⊕P^m and P^t≅P⊕P^s, and maps r:P^m→P, c:P→P^s, d:P^m→P^s, under which f is the block matrix ((p,r p),(c,d)).

source.place: Section 6.8, Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(1): integral coefficient framework and kernel-closure application; the displayed continuous-function pivot argument is an agent reduction, not a matrix argument written out in Lemma 6.8.7

proof.text: The indices i and j exclude zero ranks. For positive rank use j.succAbove and i.succAbove to enumerate the complements of the selected indices. Define a split isomorphism by projecting to the selected summand and to all complementary summands. Its inverse is the corresponding biproduct desc; verify the two identities on inclusions and projections, using succAboveCases.

Take m=n-1 and s=t-1. Define r as the biproduct desc of the q-values on complementary source indices. Define c and d by composing f with the selected source inclusion and the complementary source inclusion respectively, followed by the complementary target projection.

Check the four blocks. The selected-selected block is p by construction. The complementary-selected block is r followed by p by the equations q_k p=ι_k f π_i and finite-biproduct extensionality. The other two blocks are c and d by construction. Binary-biproduct extensionality gives the full matrix equality.

lean.statement:
theorem finiteBiproduct_pivot {P : C} {n t : ℕ}
    (f : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n ↦ P) ⟶ ⨁ fun _ : Fin t ↦ P)
    (i : Fin t) (j : Fin n)
    (q : Fin n → (P ⟶ P))
    (hq : ∀ k, q k ≫ (biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n ↦ P) j ≫ f ≫
      biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin t ↦ P) i) =
      biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n ↦ P) k ≫ f ≫ biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin t ↦ P) i) :
    ∃ (m s : ℕ), m < n ∧
      ∃ (eA : (⨁ fun _ : Fin n ↦ P) ≅ P ⊞ (⨁ fun _ : Fin m ↦ P))
        (eB : (⨁ fun _ : Fin t ↦ P) ≅ P ⊞ (⨁ fun _ : Fin s ↦ P))
        (r : (⨁ fun _ : Fin m ↦ P) ⟶ P)
        (c : P ⟶ ⨁ fun _ : Fin s ↦ P)
        (d : (⨁ fun _ : Fin m ↦ P) ⟶ ⨁ fun _ : Fin s ↦ P),
        eA.inv ≫ f ≫ eB.hom =
          biprod.lift
            (biprod.desc (biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n ↦ P) j ≫ f ≫
      biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin t ↦ P) i)
              (r ≫ (biproduct.ι (fun _ : Fin n ↦ P) j ≫ f ≫
      biproduct.π (fun _ : Fin t ↦ P) i)))
            (biprod.desc c d)
